history.summary: A popular Mariamman shrine (Nellukadai = 'paddy shop') at Melakottaivasal, Nagapattinam, administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department (temple code TM014723). Legend says a paddy trader saw the goddess in a dream and built the temple at an ant hill under a neem tree; an alternate version tells of a trader sheltering a woman who turned into a Mariamman idol. The presiding deity sits in veerasanam holding drum, rope, knife and skull. Famous for the Chedil festival, where devotees under vow are suspended by hooks on a rotating sweep. (VERIFY: no reliable source dates the temple's construction; opening hours differ across listings.)

name: Nellukadai Mariamman Temple
town_description: Nagapattinam is a coastal port town and district headquarters on the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu, with a fishing harbour and a Chola-era maritime past. It is a multi-faith pilgrimage hub — the Kayarohanaswamy and Soundararajaperumal temples, the Nagore Dargah and the nearby Velankanni church — about 25-80 km from Thanjavur and linked by rail and the East Coast Road.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport is the nearest major airport (verify distance)
travel.railway: Nagapattinam Junction, about 0.5 km from the temple (1, Perumal E Street, Melakottaivasal)
travel.road: In the heart of Nagapattinam town on the East Coast Road; town buses and autos serve the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Chittirai (Apr-May) for the Chedil festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx: Sunday 6:00 AM-9:00 PM; Mon-Sat 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 5:00-9:00 PM (VERIFY: listings differ)
